subject: Post-demo follow-up: unit-rate targets & host comparisons
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: James Ng <james.ng@bluesage.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo follow-up: unit-rate targets & host comparisons

Thanks again for the time this morning, James — appreciate the candid feedback and the product walk-through. Quick recap + asks so we can put the pricing matrix together for BlueSage: 

1) Volumes and mix (you gave roughs during the call):
   - Expected steady-state monthly tokens: ~150M tokens/month (gen-heavy).
   - Embedding/semantic search traffic: ~15M tokens/month.
   - Burst days: up to ~1.5x baseline for short windows.

2) SLOs / perf:
   - P95 latency target for generation: ~450ms (interactive user flows)
   - Offline batch/embeddings latency tolerant up to several seconds

3) Constraints:
   - SOC2 compliance required for production
   - Prefer US-only data residency for keys/logs

4) Budget signals you mentioned:
   - Internal target budget range: $30k–$50k / month initially (POC -> pilot)
   - You called out a target unit price band of roughly $200–$300 per 1M tokens as reasonable to be competitive vs current vendor spend

Next steps I propose:
- I attached a short pricing matrix (BS-pricing-matrix.xlsx) with a baseline Redwood proposal and line-item comparisons vs OpenAI, Anthropic, and a representative set of open-model hosts.
- If you confirm the volumes above and whether embeddings are in/out of scope for the pilot, we’ll produce a formal pilot quote (include pilot discounts, ingress/egress notes, and expected token uplift discounts).
- Suggested alignment call: Thursday 5/16 10am PT — go over the matrix and legal/PO path.

If anything above is off, flag it and I’ll update the sheet. I copied Laura (CS lead) to loop in SOC2 and pilot-run playbook.

Best,

Camila Reyes
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198
Redwood Inference — Production-first LLM inference

Attachments: BS-pricing-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood-vs-hosts-1M-comparison.pdf (summary)
From: James Ng <james.ng@bluesage.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Patel <sara.patel@bluesage.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 15:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: unit-rate targets & host comparisons

Thanks Camila — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Volumes: 150M/month steady-state is correct for text generation. Embeddings are likely to be out-of-scope for the initial pilot, but we'll want those in production in Q4.
- Budget: the $30k–$50k/month band is what I can push for the pilot. For long-term procurement we would need to get closer to the $40k/month midpoint or better.
- Unit economics: the internal finance team has modeled a target price range of $200–$300 per 1M tokens to make the unit economics work for our UI-heavy flows. If Redwood can show effective $/1M in that band (accounting for your caching/quantization suggestions) that would be compelling.

Two asks for the matrix:
1) Can you show an apples-to-apples comparison vs: OpenAI (gpt-4o-like spec), Anthropic (Claude-like), and two open-host providers (one managed, one self-hosted benchmark)? Please call out assumptions: context window, avg prompt+completion token ratio, and any caching that was modeled.
2) Can you include a proposed pilot price (30 day) with a clear definition of what we measure (latency, token count, error rate) and an exit path?

Also: SOC2 evidence is a hard requirement for production. If you can send the SOC2 report and any data-flow diagrams for the private-key handling we’ll accelerate the security review.

Happy to join the 5/16 call. Thursday 10am PT works.

—James
VP Engineering | BlueSage Analytics
james.ng@bluesage.ai | +1 (415) 555-1001
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: James Ng <james.ng@bluesage.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Sara Patel <sara.patel@bluesage.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 May 2028 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: unit-rate targets & host comparisons

Appreciate the clarity, James — here's a brief executive summary from the matrix I attached and the assumptions we used. I’ll walk through the full spreadsheet on Thursday but putting the headline numbers here so you have them before the call.

Assumptions (apples-to-apples):
- Average prompt + completion per request: 1.6k tokens
- Mix: 90% generation, 10% embeddings (for long-term model) — pilot excludes embeddings
- Context window modeled: 8k tokens equivalent
- Caching: conservative prefix cache on 20% of requests; we show an aggressive cache scenario (40%) in the sheet

Headline $/1M tokens (normalized; illustrative):
- OpenAI (gpt-4o-like): $980 / 1M tokens (baseline public list pricing for high-capacity generation)
- Anthropic (Claude-like): $760 / 1M tokens
- Representative managed open-host: $360 / 1M tokens
- Representative self-host (on-prem + infra amortized): $280 / 1M tokens

Redwood proposal (post-volume discounts + caching + batching):
- Pilot quote (30 days, onboarding, single-region hosted): $375 / 1M tokens (pilot discount applied)
- Committed reserved capacity (150M/month band): $220 / 1M tokens

Notes:
- The delta vs OpenAI/Anthropic is primarily model-licensing/infra cost at high quality; our competitive advantage vs managed open-hosts is predictable latency, integrated KV/prefix caching, and observability (so the effective cost after quality regressions is lower).
- We show sensitivity scenarios in the attached PDF (redwood-vs-hosts-1M-comparison.pdf) — e.g., with 40% cache and aggressive quantization the committed price can approach $160–$180 / 1M for large sustained commitments.

Next steps for Thursday:
- Walk the spreadsheet: confirm assumptions and caching modeling
- Pilot definition: confirm success metrics (we suggest P95 latency <=600ms, token delta <5% vs baseline on quality evals)
- Legal & SOC2: I attached our SOC2 snapshot and a short note on key management options (KMS/HSM) for US-only residency. Laura will lead the security handoff.

If that looks broadly aligned I’ll convert the pilot row into a formal SOW and include the billing cadence and cancellation terms.

Thanks — talk Thursday.

Camila Reyes
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
